findings.title: Groww F&O contract reader accepts a zero strike and several spellings of one strike, which D-1311 and the lake reader both refuse
findings.rule: correctness; D-1311 (an option strike must be positive); CLAUDE.md §4 (no fallback that hides a failure); §3 rule 3 (one instrument identity per contract)
findings.scenario: In the HTTP F&O discovery path (chain.rs:379 calls read_contract), the strike token goes through fno::paisa_of, which is now just crate::csv::paisa. csv::paisa accepts "0" and returns Some(0), so read_contract("NSE-NIFTY-27Mar25-0-CE", 2025-03-27) returns Some(Found) with strike Paisa(0), and Contract::of renders it as the contract "2025-03-27-0-CE". chain.rs:409 pushes it as a real contract instead of putting it in `unreadable`. The other two strike readers both refuse this. core::vendor::parse_strike (vendor.rs:1836, `Ok(strike) if strike > Paisa::ZERO`) refuses any strike at or below zero (D-1311: 'a strike is a price level, and a level at or below zero is not one'). lake::contract::parse_strike refuses "0" and any leading zero. There is a second effect: csv::paisa also reads "019200", "19200.", "19200.0" and "19200.00" all as 1_920_000. Names such as NSE-NIFTY-27Mar25-19200-CE and NSE-NIFTY-27Mar25-019200-CE therefore pass chain.rs's name-level `seen_names` dedup as two different names, yet both resolve to the same InstrumentKey. That is two vendor series filed under one contract, which is the non-injective aliasing lake::contract::parse_strike refuses for exactly this reason. No test in fno.rs covers a zero or non-canonical strike: its paisa_of tests cover only signed and fractional values (lines 680-692).
findings.evidence: crates/pull/src/fno.rs:1191 `let strike = brutex_core::price::Paisa::from_raw(paisa_of(strike)?);` (no positivity or canonical-form check); crates/pull/src/fno.rs:1268-1280 `fn paisa_of(text: &str) -> Option<i64> { ... crate::csv::paisa(text) }`; crates/pull/src/csv.rs:397-413 `let (whole, frac) = text.split_once('.').unwrap_or((text, "")); ... let rupees: i64 = digits.parse().ok()?; ... let total = rupees.checked_mul(100)?.checked_add(hundredths)?;` (accepts "0", leading zeros and an empty or zero fraction); contrast crates/core/src/vendor.rs:1836 `Ok(strike) if strike > Paisa::ZERO => Ok(strike),` and crates/lake/src/contract.rs:351 `if text.starts_with('0') { return Err(bad()); }`

findings.title: A pipelined client that stops reading responses holds its connection slot forever; 256 of them stop the server accepting and block Ctrl-C shutdown
findings.rule: security (slowloris/connection exhaustion); the stated purpose of MAX_CONNECTIONS / HEAD_READ_TIMEOUT / BODY_READ_TIMEOUT (D-1200, D-1510)
findings.scenario:
A local client opens a connection to the loopback listener. In a single write it sends several thousand pipelined `GET /vocab.json HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:PORT

` requests (or `/health`), then never reads from the socket. Responses pile up until the socket send and receive buffers are full, and hyper's poll_flush returns Pending. The remaining pipelined requests are still in hyper's read_buf. Two hyper paths then return Pending without touching the IO: hyper-1.11.0 conn.rs:495 (`if self.state.allow_half_close || !self.io.read_buf().is_empty() { return Poll::Pending; }`) and dispatch.rs:627 (`if self.in_flight.is_some() { Poll::Pending }`). So HeadDeadline::poll_read is never called. That function is the only place the alarm is polled (server.rs:17916-17922), and poll_write (17940/17953) has no deadline at all. The state can also be HeadState::Delivered, which has no alarm. Either way the Slot is never dropped. Repeat this on 256 connections (MAX_CONNECTIONS, 17543) and `LimitedListener::accept` waits in `while !self.slots.try_take()` (17729) forever, so every real request from the operator's browser hangs. The same stuck connection also blocks shutdown. `serve_limited` uses `axum::serve(listener, app).with_graceful_shutdown(..)` (18033), and axum-0.8.9 serve/mod.rs:303 waits on `close_tx.closed().await` with no timeout. Ctrl-C therefore never returns from `serve`, `run` never returns, and main never reaches `end_runtime`/SHUTDOWN_GRACE. docs/06-limits.md 'Slow clients' bounds slow heads and slow bodies but never mentions slow readers, so this is not a documented limit.

findings.title: An interim `100 Continue` re-arms the head deadline, so an Expect request whose handler runs past 10 s is killed mid-handler with a false 408
findings.rule: correctness (a fallback that hides a failure / wrong refusal, CLAUDE.md §4)
findings.scenario: An admitted local client (Host 127.0.0.1:PORT, Origin http://127.0.0.1:PORT) sends `POST /universe/resolve` with `Expect: 100-continue` and the body `feed=dhan`. Hyper writes `HTTP/1.1 100 Continue` when the body is first polled (hyper-1.11.0 conn.rs:410-413). That write goes through HeadDeadline::poll_write, which calls rearm() (server.rs:17940), so the connection returns to HeadState::Awaiting with a fresh 10 s deadline. The body bytes then arrive, and observe() (17810) scans them as if they were a new request head: they contain no blank line, so the state stays Awaiting with partial=true. The handler then runs `pull::resolve::crawl` inline (server.rs:34474, about 300 HTTP fetches), which takes well over 10 s. Meanwhile hyper's dispatcher polls the read side (mid_message_detect_eof with an empty read_buf), so HeadDeadline::poll_read sees the deadline pass (17903). expire(true) writes `408 ... the request head did not arrive in time` into the socket in the middle of the exchange (17883) and returns TimedOut. Hyper drops the connection and the in-flight handler future, which aborts the crawl. The client, whose head did arrive, gets a 408 that names the wrong cause, and the real answer is lost. docs/06-limits.md names only the pipelined-second-request variant of this.

findings.title: A whole-number `limit` too large for usize is treated as 'not a whole number' and answered with the default instead of being clamped to the ceiling
findings.rule: correctness (documented contract: 'Clamped rather than refused: a bookmarked ?limit=99999 ... the honest answer is everything up to the ceiling')
findings.scenario: `GET /backtest.json?limit=99999999999999999999` (20 digits). `parse::<usize>()` fails with an overflow error, so unparseable_limit emits the Warn `limit ignored` with 'not a whole number; answered the default page', and limit_asked returns DEFAULT_LIMIT=500 instead of MAX_RUNS=20000. The operator asked for everything and gets 500 rows, and the log calls a whole number not a whole number. `/logs` and `/logs.json` have the same shape (logs.rs:143-146: `.parse::<usize>().unwrap_or(50).clamp(1, PAGE_LIMIT)`): an overflowing limit gives 50, not PAGE_LIMIT=200.

findings.title: Walk-forward folds search at a support threshold derived from the whole span, test windows included
findings.rule: CLAUDE.md §3 rule 7 (no look-ahead). The repo applies this rule to walk-forward folds itself: GAP4-46 / D-1660, lib.rs:6119-6124, says a whole-span parameter reaching a fold is 'exactly' what rule 7 bans.
findings.scenario: Run range-all / one_rung with no named support (support_ppm = None) and validation on. That is the default: validate_from_env() returns true when BRUTEX_VALIDATE is unset. min_hits = max(affordable_min_hits(&column, ...), statistical). affordable_min_hits runs Sweeper::auto over the column built from the WHOLE span, finding the deepest threshold whose Apriori walk completes under the probe ceiling. That threshold depends on how many combinations are frequent across every bar, including the bars in each fold's TEST window. The value goes into ladder_for(min_hits), then into both_shapes(..., ladder, ...), then into walk_forward_core. There, fold_ladder(base, train.len(), bars.len()) rescales base.min_hits() by the length ratio. So fold 0 (trained on bars 0..t0) sweeps at a threshold set partly by bars after t0. Changing bars only in the last fold's test window so more conditions co-occur pushes Sweeper::auto to a higher affordable threshold. Every earlier fold's per_fold min_hits then rises, its training sweep finds a different (smaller) candidate set, and its chosen candidate and FoldResult can change. LBD-01's test (a_test_window_bar_cannot_move_an_earlier_folds_exit_ladder) proves this property only for the rung count, using a fixed ladder. Nothing tests it for the support threshold on the production path.

findings.title: A stop stated in points is converted at the whole-span price midpoint, so each trade's stop depends on later bars and is not the stated number of points
findings.rule: CLAUDE.md §3 rule 7 (no look-ahead), plus a wrong result against the function's own documented contract
findings.scenario: Set BRUTEX_MAX_STOP_POINTS=50 and run any range verb, or screen/elite with MAX_POINTS through ceiling_in_ppm, over NIFTY 2020-01..2026-08. reference_price takes (min low + max high)/2 over the whole span. The repo's own measurement is about 1,694,272 paisa, giving 2951 ppm. Excursions are measured in ppm of each trade's own entry (excursion::ppm_of), so the stop actually applied is 2951 ppm of the entry. At a 25,000.00 entry that is about 73.8 points; at the March-2020 low near 7,600 it is about 22.4 points, not 50. The stop on a 2020 trade also depends on bars that come after it. Extend `to` by one month that sets a new all-time high: max high rises, reference rises, ppm falls, and the stop and admission of trades years earlier change. Rules::derived puts this ppm into max_mae_ppm, which feeds Levels::forced and admission, so the earlier trade's priced cell and pass/fail move with future prices.

findings.title: Gate 1 'orphans' counts conventional crate targets as compiled even when Cargo's auto-discovery or a target path override means nothing compiles them
findings.rule: CLAUDE.md section 2 (Rust is the only language; gate 1 claims 'every .rs outside web/ is compiled'): a gate that can pass while its rule is broken
findings.scenario: Add `autotests = false` under [package] in crates/core/Cargo.toml, which no gate refuses. git grep for autotests/autobins/autobenches/autoexamples/autolib in .github/ finds nothing. Then track crates/core/tests/tool.rs containing `import os` / `os.system("echo hi")`. That text is UTF-8, has no NUL and no shebang, and lexes as Rust tokens, so `content` passes it. compiled_roots still makes it a root (member + tests/*.rs), so `orphans` prints no ORPHAN. Cargo never discovers the target, so build, test and clippy stay green. Gate 1 then prints 'every .rs outside web/ is compiled' over a Python file. `[lib] path = "src/engine.rs"` does the same thing to a tracked src/lib.rs, and `[[test]] required-features` does it to a tests file. Gate 14 already handles the required-features case for benches only.
findings.evidence:
.github/source_scan.rs:3104-3116 at origin/final/all-fixes:
            [".github", _] => built.contains(f),
            ["crates", c, "build.rs"] => member(c),
            ["crates", c, "src", "lib.rs" | "main.rs"] => member(c),
            ...
            ["crates", c, "tests" | "benches" | "examples", file] => {
                member(c) && file.ends_with(".rs")
            }
The only manifest keys read are `[t, "path"] | [t, "build"]` (line ~3123); auto*-discovery flags and lib/bin path overrides of the conventional file are never consulted.

findings.title: A ✓ invariant row written without a trailing pipe skips the 'names a proof' check and bare-name resolution
findings.rule: Gate 10 / P12-02 (D-1799): every ✓ row in docs/04-invariants.md must name a test, gate or front-end test file; a ledger/invariant check must not skip rows
findings.scenario: Add the row `| X-99 | a property | the same test's second half | ✓` with no closing `|`. GFM renders this as a normal table row. row_cells pushes a cell only when it meets a `|`, so it returns [" X-99 ", " a property ", " the same test's second half "]. That is 3 cells, so the len<3 guard does not skip the row, but `status` is now the proof cell, which is not "✓". unproven_ticks therefore never refuses it, and bare_proof_names returns nothing for it. The same row with a trailing `|` is refused (the test at line 954 asserts exactly that). gates_ledger gate 10 only checks backticked a::b::c tokens, so an unproven ✓ row passes every gate.

findings.title: names_a_proof accepts any word ending in 'gate' followed by a digit as naming a CI gate
findings.rule: Gate 10 / P12-02 (D-1799): a ✓ row's proof cell must name a test, a gate by number, or a .test.js file
findings.scenario: Row `| X-99 | a property | the aggregate 3 rows | ✓ |`. Lowercased, the cell contains "gate 3" inside "aggregate 3", so match_indices("gate ") hits and a digit follows. names_a_proof returns true, and the row passes even though it names no test, gate or file. The same happens with "delegate 2", "propagate 1" and "navigate 4". The suite's own negative case "the aggregate count" is refused only because no digit follows, which shows the substring match is unintended.

findings.title: Gate 18 with --build-timeout-multiplier 2 (commit 46439dee) can report a correct mutant as TIMEOUT: one build bound is taken from a baseline run alone and applied to the second worker's cold first build, which runs alongside worker 1
findings.rule: correctness (gate result): a mutant the tests would catch must not be reported as a failure
findings.scenario: In cargo-mutants 26.2.0, timeouts.rs:80-96 sets build = baseline Build-phase duration × 2, once. lab.rs:69-73 applies that one value to every mutant on every thread (lab.rs:282-285). The baseline runs alone in build dir 0 (lab.rs:51,71). The second --jobs worker gets a fresh BuildDir::copy_from (lab.rs:107), and copy_tree leaves out target/ because copy_target defaults to false (options.rs:358-359, copy_tree.rs:105). Its first mutant build is therefore a full cold build of the mutated package's tests. That build does at most the baseline's work (the baseline builds the union of the shard's mutated packages, lab.rs:180-190) but runs at the same moment as worker 1's rebuild and test phase. Both share the 4 vCPUs and the 4-token jobserver (`--jobs 2 --jobserver-tasks 4`), and worker 1's test processes (RAYON_NUM_THREADS=2) hold no jobserver tokens. Take a shard whose mutants are all in one heavy crate, say cli. The baseline cold-builds cli in time T with the machine to itself. Worker 2 cold-builds the same cli test set while worker 1 recompiles and relinks cli. If worker 2 gets less than half the throughput the baseline had, its build passes 2T. process.rs:122-126 then kills it and returns Exit::Timeout. outcome.rs classifies that as Timeout, not Unviable, because is_failure() is false for Timeout. The mutant goes into timeout.txt, and mutation_gate verify refuses the shard (`!timeout.is_empty()`). Nothing in the source extends or exempts the first build of a new build dir. So a correct mutant can be reported TIMEOUT whenever contention more than halves worker 2's build rate. That is a false red, not a false green: the mutant is never credited as caught. origin/final/all-fixes does not carry the flag, so it has no build bound; an endless const-eval build there runs to the 240-minute job limit and fails closed.

findings.title: Coverage gate passes at 90% lines / 89% regions and measures no branch coverage, while CLAUDE.md section 9 requires 100% line and branch coverage
findings.rule: CLAUDE.md section 9: 'line and branch coverage 100% on every touched crate'; CLAUDE.md section 10: where this file and a document disagree, this file wins
findings.scenario: A change that leaves 9% of the lines in a touched crate uncovered, and any number of branches untested, turns the coverage job green as long as the workspace-wide totals stay at or above 90/89. ci-ok then reports green. No `--branch` flag is passed anywhere, so branch coverage is never measured. Gate 20 holds a declared-uncovered list for crates/telemetry only. The workflow comment admits that section 9's 100% 'IS NOT ENFORCED HERE'. CLAUDE.md was never amended, so the law and the gate disagree, and no gate enforces the stated rule.

findings.title: Recovery reconciliation appends pending attempts to the shared and plan journals in HashMap (RandomState) iteration order, so identical reruns write different journal bytes
findings.rule: CLAUDE.md §3 rule 5 (idempotence: same inputs, same outputs, byte for byte)
findings.scenario: Two pending attempts A and B are both Queued, InFlight or Unverified in the shared attempts journal, and each reassesses to a changed state (`reassessed` returns Some). On one process `attempts.latest.values()` yields A then B, so `append_attempt` writes A's record and then B's record to both the shared journal and the plan journal. On a rerun over byte-identical journals and store, `std::collections::HashMap`'s per-process RandomState can yield B then A, so the appended records land in the opposite order and the two journal files differ byte for byte. The early `?` exits inside the loop make it worse: `checked(&item.body, today)?`, `stored_scope_key(&item.body)?`, the 'shared attempt has invalid identity' Err, and `append_attempt(...)?`. When one row refuses, the set of rows already appended before the abort is a hash-order-dependent prefix, so two identical runs can leave different partial journal states. `Journal` already carries `order: Vec<[u8; 32]>`, documented as 'Distinct work keys in first-appearance order, stable across restart', and this loop ignores it. Nothing sorts `pending` afterwards. The test at recovery.rs:2820 documents the same HashMap-order hazard for `validate_seal`, which `scope_order` fixes there, but the hazard is not handled here.

findings.title: Bar-window change reason says 'previous close/OI is zero' for any non-positive base, including a corrupt negative value
findings.rule: CLAUDE.md section 4: a fallback that hides a failure (degrade loudly and NAME THE REASON). server::Unknown's own doc: 'Five reasons, five different sentences on screen ... collapsing distinct facts is the fallback section 4 bans'
findings.scenario: basis_points refuses any base <= 0 as Unknown::BaseNotPositive (server.rs:4387 `if first_paisa <= 0 { return Err(Unknown::BaseNotPositive) }`). Its own doc (server.rs ~4376) says bars::with_change passes raw stored values and 'a store read does not validate prices (an unsealed month is read with no checksum). One corrupt bar of i64::MIN ...'. with_change matches only Overflow and sends every other Err to the zero label. So a previous bar whose stored close is -100 or i64::MIN gives chg_why = "previous_close_zero". The page (web/src/routes/db/+page.svelte BAR_WHY) then renders 'the previous close is zero paisa'. That is false: the close is negative, which means the stored data is corrupt. The same happens for open interest at line 729: a previous OI of -1 (negative but not the OI_NULL sentinel) gives "previous_oi_zero" ('the previous open interest is zero'). The correct, distinct code base_not_positive already exists (server.rs:4326) and is not used. No test covers a negative base on this route. bars_window_route_tests.rs:252 pins only the zero-OI case.

findings.title: Build staleness check reports 'serving' (no source newer) when the source walk was truncated or hit an unreadable directory
findings.rule: CLAUDE.md section 4: a fallback that hides a failure. Build::read's own doc: 'a comparison that cannot be made is not evidence of freshness or of staleness'
findings.scenario: newest_under walks web/src, but it silently `continue`s past any directory whose read_dir fails and any entry whose file_type or mtime fails, and it silently `break`s once `seen >= MAX_WALK` (100,000). None of these is counted or reported. Two examples: (a) web/src/routes is chmod 000 and holds the only edit made after the last build, or (b) the edited file lies past the 100,000th entry visited (for example a node_modules tree under src). In both cases the newest timestamp found is older than build/index.html, so Build::read returns Build::Serving. Build::Serving is documented as 'A shell is there, and no source is newer than it', so the banner and log state 'serving' over a stale bundle. The doc forbids reporting an incomplete comparison as a fresh one. The sibling walk in the same file (line 406/417) counts `tree.unreadable` for exactly this reason, and this walk does not.

findings.title: Census entry decoder applies version-3 contract meaning to version-2 entries, and turns an invalid contract into the spot key instead of refusing it
findings.rule: CLAUDE.md §3 rule 8 / docs/02-store-format.md §2 and §11.5 ('A future field takes reserved space in a new version, never by reinterpreting version 2'); §11.5a ('A length past 24, or text that does not parse as a contract, is not read as a shorter or different contract'); CLAUDE.md §4 (no fallback that hides a failure)
findings.scenario: Layout::decode_entry chooses its decoder only by carries_closes, which is true for both V2 and V3. So a version-2 census entry goes through Held::decode, which reads bytes 16..41 of the closes half as a contract. Version 2 defined those bytes as reserved, and the v2-era Held::decode (a7078e5a, manifest.rs:1585-1594) ignored them. Take a checksum-valid v2 entry with nonzero bytes there. It used to mean 'spot key'; the current build reads it as a derivative-contract key, which reinterprets version-2 bytes. Second case: a v3 entry whose contract_len byte is 30 (past CONTRACT_CAPACITY 24), or whose text does not parse. read_contract returns None, so the row loads silently as the SPOT key for that underlying and month. The index is newest-wins, so that row's `rows` count replaces the real spot month's count. This is the 'merge two series under one key' that read_contract's own doc says it prevents. Reserved bytes 41..60 of a v3 entry are also never checked for zero, unlike the bar header, which refuses a nonzero reserved tail (D-1353). Every case needs an entry whose second-half CRC was recomputed; no writer emits these bytes. This is the resealed-slot class the project already treats as a defect (D-1353/D-1354).
findings.evidence: crates/pull/src/manifest.rs:1693-1695: `pub fn decode_entry(self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Held, EntryFault> { if self.carries_closes { Held::decode(bytes)`; manifest.rs:1676-1677: `let mut entry = entry; entry.key.contract = read_contract(&half);`; manifest.rs:3423-3429: `fn read_contract(half: &[u8; IMAGE_LEN]) -> Option<Contract> { let n = usize::from(*half.get(C_CONTRACT_N)?); if n == 0 || n > C_CONTRACT_LEN { return None; } let text = core::str::from_utf8(...).ok()?; Contract::parse(text) }`; the doc above it at manifest.rs:3419-3422 says 'answers None rather than a partial name ... reading one would merge two series under one key'; docs/02-store-format.md:843: 'A length past 24, or text that does not parse as a contract, is not read as a shorter or different contract'; manifest.rs:601 `pub const V3: Self = Self::declared(3, MAGIC_V2, ENTRY_STRIDE, ENTRY_LEN, true);` and the comment at manifest.rs:504-506 says 'the format version is what tells the two apart', but the version is never consulted on decode.

findings.title: The authoritative store-format doc and Layout's own docs say the overlay and Greeks geometries are not in Layout::KNOWN; the code puts them there
findings.rule: docs/02-store-format.md is the stated authority over bytes on disk ('This document is the authority; the code follows it'); CLAUDE.md §3 rule 6 (honest limits) and §10
findings.scenario: docs/02 §8 tells a reader that `.ovl` and `.grk` are outside Layout::KNOWN, so Layout::for_version / Header::decode could never resolve version 9 or 8. In fact Layout::for_version(9) returns the 24-byte overlay geometry and Header::decode accepts a BRUTEXB9 slot. The only thing that keeps an overlay header in a `.bin` from being read at stride 24 is file.rs's per-kind BAR_TABLE (file.rs:1364, 1389-1395), and the doc does not name it. Layout::OVERLAY and Layout::GREEKS also carry '# Why it is NOT in Self::KNOWN' doc blocks that contradict the KNOWN constant a few lines later and its own '# Why the overlay is here' block. store/tests/unit.rs:888 asserts the real membership, so the code and the authority disagree and no doc test reads the sentence.
findings.evidence: docs/02-store-format.md:482: 'Neither is in `store::layout::Layout::KNOWN`, the bar versions a `.bin` resolves against.'; crates/store/src/layout.rs:124: `/// # Why it is NOT in [`Self::KNOWN`]`; layout.rs:146: `/// Not in [`Self::KNOWN`], for exactly the reason [`Self::OVERLAY`] is not`; layout.rs:192: `pub const KNOWN: &'static [Self] = &[Self::V2, Self::V3, Self::OVERLAY, Self::GREEKS];`; crates/store/tests/unit.rs:888: `assert_eq!(Layout::KNOWN, &[v2, v3, Layout::OVERLAY, Layout::GREEKS]);`
